title: The Rhythm Kings' last jobs in New Orleans
summary: He tells of two final jobs with the Rhythm Kings, their stint in Mobile, and Dave Winer.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well now where we go. I was wondering about when Mares came back from Chicago with the Rhythm Kings.

Yeah. Did he play any jobs around there? Yeah. They uh... I played two jobs. Joe's got the uh... Do you ever go around by Joe's place? Once in a while. Well he's got the ad for this one night. Well I played two nights with him. We played one night at the New Orleans Athletic Club and the other night at the Italian Hall. And it was after that that the band broke up. That's the last two jobs that they played as a band. Before that though they had gone over. They went over to Mobile and they worked over at Mobile for about... Well I guess five or six months. As the New Orleans Rhythm Kings. They had over there they had Leo Addy. Steve Lycanna. And the kid that's got the best job in Chicago and he's headed for... He just signed a... When we were up there. When I was up there with Shoggy. He just signed another ten year contract. He had been there ten years before that. At that Ambassador to the East in Chicago. You know anything about Chicago? Well that's the class job in Chicago. The Ambassador to the East. Dave Lewinners. Do you know of him? Piano player. Dave Lewinners. Dave Lewinners. He's been there... He's going on twenty years now. On that one job. Yeah. Well they sent... They sent all the way to Chicago to get Dave to come down there. And to play with them and they ain't even got a job. So he went to... He worked with Tony Peretti at the Levita. Do that. Yeah. He worked with Tony. After that they went over there and they couldn't do any good over there. They stayed over there about four, five, six months. Didn't do any good so they come back home. And Dave went to work with Tony Peretti there at the Levita and then he went back to Chicago. But that's the... That was the last two... That was the last two jobs that the Rhythm Kings played as a... As a unit. And there was Paul Rapp, Steve Loiskaner, Red Long, because Lewinners was working with Peretti. And Chink Martin. And myself. Ah, Santo. Santo Antrono.
